title: Deforestation and Forest Loss
text: Deforestation is the large-scale removal of forests, primarily driven by agriculture (particularly cattle ranching and soy production), logging, infrastructure development, and mining. Tropical forests, especially the Amazon rainforest, are under greatest pressure. Brazil's Amazon lost approximately 11,500 square kilometers of forest in 2022. Deforestation contributes approximately 10–15% of global greenhouse gas emissions through the release of carbon stored in trees. It also causes loss of biodiversity, soil erosion, disruption of water cycles, and displacement of indigenous communities. Global efforts to combat deforestation include REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation) under the UNFCCC.
